title: NHS Graduate Management Training Scheme 2027: Applications Open for Future NHS Leaders
summary: Applications are now open for the NHS Graduate Management Training Scheme (GMTS) 2027 entry , offering graduates and eligible applicants an opportunity to develop their leadership, management and professional skills while working within the National Health Service. The NHS GMTS is designed for people who demonstrate passion, potential and leadership capability . According to the programme, its recruitment process is not focused simply on what applicants studied, which university they attended, or what previous work experience they have. Instead, the selection process is designed to assess candidates’ strengths and potential to become future NHS leaders. Applications for 2027 entry are currently open and will close on 28 October at 11:30am. Apply for the NHS Graduate Management Training Scheme 2027 What Is the NHS Graduate Management Training Scheme? The NHS Graduate Management Training Scheme (GMTS) is a structured graduate development and employment programme designed to develop future leaders within the NHS. The Scheme combines employment, professional development, academic study and practical experience. Successful applicants become full-time NHS employees rather than students on a conventional university programme. The official eligibility information states that trainees undertake at least two years of work experience, professional leadership training and academic qualifications. The programme is intended for individuals who want to build a career in healthcare management and leadership and who are interested in contributing to the delivery and improvement of health and care services. The NHS currently lists a starting salary of £31,276 , with the possibility of an increase to £33,681 after 12 months , alongside NHS employment benefits. Why Consider the NHS Graduate Management Training Scheme? The GMTS provides an opportunity to develop professional skills while gaining practical experience within the NHS. Depending on the specialism, trainees can develop experience in areas such as: General management Human resources Finance Digital and health informatics Engineering and estates management The exact academic qualification, duration and entry requirements can vary by specialism. For example, the HR pathway is listed as a two-year programme for applicants with any degree at 2:2 or above. The Scheme also provides structured support throughout the trainee journey, including programme management, placement support, educational support and access to experienced colleagues and previous trainees. NHS GMTS 2027 Recruitment Process The 2027 recruitment process consists of several stages. Applicants should be prepared to complete online assessments before progressing to the Virtual Assessment Centre. Registration and Application Form The first step is to register and complete the online application form. Applicants should ensure that they meet the relevant entry requirements before beginning the application process. The NHS specifically encourages applicants to apply early because successful candidates will need time to complete the assessment stages that follow the application. Stage 1: Future Potential Assessment The first assessment stage is the Future Potential Assessment , which takes place online. The assessment is expected to take approximately 45 minutes , although it is not time limited. This stage is designed to help applicants learn more about the type of work they could undertake on the Scheme while allowing the NHS to assess aspects of their potential. Before beginning the actual assessment, applicants will have the opportunity to practise each type of question. One important feature of the process is that all candidates receive a feedback report after completing this stage , providing information about their performance. If successful, applicants are invited to proceed to Stage 2. Stage 2: NHS GMTS Alignment Assessment Successful Stage 1 candidates can move on to the NHS GMTS Alignment Assessment . This assessment takes approximately 60 minutes . One of its main features is the inclusion of video responses , allowing candidates to demonstrate more about themselves as individuals. Applicants will have the opportunity to practise each question type before completing the assessment. Although the overall assessment takes approximately one hour, only the video-based questions are timed. Candidates also receive a feedback report after completing Stage 2. Human Review of Video Responses An important point for applicants is that the NHS GMTS states that its team manually reviews video interview responses and does not use artificial intelligence for this part of the process. Candidates should therefore focus on presenting their own experiences, motivations and examples clearly and authentically. Successful candidates proceed to the Virtual Assessment Centre. Stage 3: Virtual Assessment Centre The Virtual Assessment Centre (VAC) represents the final assessment stage of the recruitment process. VACs for the 2027 entry process are scheduled to begin in January 2027 and continue through February 2027 . The VAC is a half-day assessment involving several exercises. During the assessment, candidates will have the opportunity to: Complete a range of assessment exercises Meet members of the NHS team Interact with other candidates Demonstrate their strengths in different situations Experience the assessment environment virtually The NHS encourages applicants to be themselves throughout the process. Candidates receive a feedback report after the VAC regardless of the outcome. Possible VAC Outcomes Following the Virtual Assessment Centre, candidates can receive one of three outcomes: Successful at VAC – an immediate offer will be made. Reserve list – the candidate may be contacted if a place on the Scheme becomes available. Unsuccessful at VAC – the candidate will not progress to an offer. The VAC is the final assessment stage. Placement allocation happens afterwards and is separate from the assessment process. Placement Allocation Candidates who successfully pass the VAC and receive an offer then enter the allocation process . Allocation involves matching successful candidates with available placements within NHS organisations. The NHS considers factors including: Assessment scores Candidate preferences Available placement roles Regional considerations Personal circumstances where applicable The NHS states that it will endeavour to match individuals with the closest possible placement based on their indicated preferences. However, a preferred region cannot necessarily be guaranteed because placement availability and other factors affect the allocation process. This means applicants should consider flexibility when thinking about potential placement locations. Offer and Onboarding Candidates who successfully pass the VAC and are matched with a placement will receive an offer to join the Scheme. The next stage involves: Pre-employment checks Qualification verification Immigration/right-to-work checks where applicable Onboarding Preparation for employment Successful candidates are expected to be ready to join the Scheme on the first Monday of September 2027 . Preparation Materials for Applicants The NHS GMTS provides preparation resources throughout the assessment process. Once an applicant applies, relevant preparation materials become available in their account at each stage. For Stage 1 and Stage 2 , applicants can access: Hints and tips videos Practice tests Examples similar to the actual assessments Opportunities to practise question types For the Virtual Assessment Centre , preparation support includes: Coaching calls Hints and tips Platform familiarisation videos Applicants are not required to complete all preparation materials. However, the NHS encourages candidates to use them because they can help applicants become familiar with the assessment process. The online practice assessments can also be used to test equipment and internet connections before completing the actual assessments. The VAC platform has its own technical-check function, allowing candidates to check that their microphone and camera are working correctly. Reasonable Adjustments During the Recruitment Process The NHS GMTS recognises that applicants may require reasonable adjustments during the recruitment process. Applicants are encouraged to disclose their adjustment needs if they require additional support. The programme states that disclosure is a personal decision and that applicants do not need to provide information they prefer to keep private. The recruitment team only needs sufficient information to understand what adjustments are required. The VAC team may also ask whether there are medical conditions that need to be considered in order to provide appropriate support. The stated objective is to ensure that candidates can participate in the selection process comfortably and fairly. Fair and Inclusive Assessment The NHS GMTS states that assessors receive training designed to support a fair and inclusive recruitment process. This training includes recognising and avoiding unconscious bias . The programme describes its approach as being committed to an equitable assessment experience for candidates. The NHS s eligibility information also states its commitment to equality of opportunity and says that candidates should not receive less favourable treatment on grounds including age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage or civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, sex, or sexual orientation. NHS Graduate Management Training Scheme Entry Requirements Applicants should carefully check the requirements for their preferred specialism because requirements differ for some pathways. For General Management, Human Resources, Finance and Digital – Health Informatics , the standard minimum requirement is a 2:2 degree in any subject . The NHS also recognises certain alternative qualifications, including: A postgraduate qualification such as an MBA, Master s or PhD Certain health- or management-related degree-level equivalent qualifications NVQ Level 5 in Management Diploma in Management Studies Diploma in Nursing, Midwifery or Health Visiting Diploma from the Chartered Society of Physiotherapy Diploma in Speech and Language Therapy Diploma from the College of Occupational Therapy Diploma from the College of Radiographers Diploma in Social Work or Certificate of Qualification in Social Work Certain qualifications are specifically listed as not acceptable, including a Certificate in Management Studies, general DipHE qualifications outside the accepted list, ONC/OND, HNC/HND, CGLI/C G and certain operating department certificates or diplomas. Engineering and Estates Management Requirements The Engineering and Estates Management (EEM) pathway has different academic requirements. Applicants need at least a 2:2 degree in an appropriate engineering discipline , including: Mechanical Engineering Electrical Engineering Building Services Engineering The degree must be accredited by the Engineering Council for the relevant standard route to professional chartership. The NHS also notes that applicants holding an MEng, whether through a BEng plus Master s or a structured four-year MEng, are not eligible for the Estates Engineering Management specialism. Right to Work in the United Kingdom One of the most important requirements for applicants is the right to work in the UK. All candidates must have the right to work in the UK for the entire duration of the Scheme. The NHS GMTS is a full-time employment programme rather than a student programme. Applicants are responsible for ensuring that they have the appropriate immigration status or visa to work in the UK for the complete duration of the Scheme. If an applicant does not have the required right to work, their application or offer may be withdrawn. Offers are subject to pre-employment checks, which can include: Immigration status verification Qualification verification Recent proof of address in the UK Other employment checks The NHS notes that immigration requirements can change and that applicants should ensure their status allows them to undertake the full programme. Is Previous Work Experience Required? The NHS GMTS does not require specific work experience as an eligibility condition. This is important because the Scheme s recruitment approach focuses on potential rather than simply selecting applicants based on their previous employment history. However, the NHS states that tangible examples of work experience, whether paid or unpaid, can be useful during the interview and assessment process. Examples could include volunteering or other activities that demonstrate skills, initiative, teamwork, leadership, communication or an understanding of healthcare. For example, the NHS notes that volunteering at a local hospital can provide useful experience and help an applicant better understand the challenges facing NHS services. Can Current NHS Employees Apply? Yes. The NHS Graduate Management Training Scheme is open to current NHS employees, who are referred to as in-service trainees . Current NHS staff must still meet the same academic eligibility and right-to-work requirements as other applicants. There are no academic eligibility exceptions simply because someone already works for the NHS. The recruitment and assessment process is also the same for current NHS employees and external applicants. Current NHS employees who are successful may have their previous reckonable NHS service considered as part of the employment process. Final-Year Students Can Apply Students who have just started their final year of a degree can apply, provided they meet the relevant requirements. The NHS states that final-year students must have obtained their final confirmed degree classification, with a minimum of 2:2, by mid-August 2027 . Successful candidates then join the Scheme on the first Monday of September 2027. This makes the 2027 intake relevant to students who are currently approaching the final stage of their undergraduate studies as well as graduates who already hold their qualifications. No Age Limit There is no age limit for applying to the NHS Graduate Management Training Scheme. The NHS states that applicants who meet the minimum entry requirements, have an interest in health and care, and consider the GMTS an appropriate career move are welcome to apply. What Happens After Completing the Scheme? During the Scheme, trainees are employed on a fixed-term contract. The NHS states that trainees undertake work experience, professional leadership training and academic qualifications. Depending on the specialism, the employment period can be 24 or 30 months . The Scheme is intended to support participants in progressing into NHS careers after completing their training. The NHS reports that the average salary earned by trainees in their first NHS role after completing the Scheme is around £44,000 , although actual salaries vary according to the role obtained. The programme does not guarantee a particular job after completion, but the NHS GMTS provides support with finding a first substantive NHS position, including job-search advice through its support network. Salary and Benefits The current NHS GMTS information lists a minimum starting salary of £31,276 , with a potential increase after 12 months. Depending on placement location, a High Cost Area Supplement may also apply. Other benefits include access to the NHS Pension Scheme and employee support programmes. The Scheme s published information also highlights benefits such as: NHS Pension Scheme Employee Assistance Programme Cycle2Work scheme Employment within the NHS Structured professional development Academic study Leadership training Placement experience Support from programme and placement teams Current NHS employees may have different salary arrangements depending on their existing NHS employment and recognised service. Key Features of the NHS GMTS 2027 Opportunity For applicants considering the programme, the main features include: 2027 entry to the NHS Graduate Management Training Scheme Applications currently open Minimum 2:2 degree for most specialisms Degree can be in any subject for General Management, HR, Finance and Digital – Health Informatics Separate engineering degree requirements for Engineering and Estates Management No specific previous work experience required No age limit Current NHS employees can apply Final-year students can apply if they meet the qualification deadline Full-time employment during the Scheme Professional leadership development Academic qualifications Practical NHS work experience Online assessments Virtual Assessment Centre Placement allocation following successful assessment Structured preparation materials Feedback following assessment stages Reasonable adjustment support Trained assessors UK right-to-work requirement NHS GMTS 2027 Application Timeline Applicants should be aware of the key dates and stages associated with the 2027 intake. Application deadline 28 October 2026 at 11:30am Stage 1 Future Potential Assessment completed online following successful registration and application. Stage 2 Successful Stage 1 candidates proceed to the NHS GMTS Alignment Assessment, including video responses. January–February 2027 Virtual Assessment Centres are scheduled to take place. September 2027 Successful candidates who complete the assessment, placement matching and onboarding process are expected to begin the Scheme on the first Monday of September 2027 . How to Apply for the NHS Graduate Management Training Scheme 2027 Applicants should first review the eligibility requirements for the specialism they wish to pursue. Step 1: Check eligibility Confirm that you have: The required academic qualification The appropriate qualification for your chosen specialism The right to work in the UK for the entire Scheme Any additional requirements relevant to your pathway Step 2: Complete the application Applications are submitted through the NHS GMTS application system. NHS GMTS 2027 Application Portal Step 3: Complete Stage 1 If your application progresses, complete the Future Potential Assessment. Use the available practice materials to familiarise yourself with the question formats. Step 4: Complete Stage 2 Successful Stage 1 applicants move to the NHS GMTS Alignment Assessment, including video responses. Step 5: Attend the Virtual Assessment Centre Candidates who successfully pass the online assessment stages are invited to the half-day VAC. Step 6: Placement allocation Successful candidates are matched with available NHS placements according to the Scheme s allocation process. Step 7: Pre-employment checks and onboarding Candidates who are successfully matched complete the necessary checks and onboarding before joining the Scheme. Tips for Preparing Your Application Although the NHS GMTS does not require applicants to have a particular academic subject or specific work history for most pathways, applicants should still prepare carefully. 1. Understand the pathway you are applying for Read the requirements for your chosen specialism carefully. The standard requirements do not apply identically to every pathway, particularly Engineering and Estates Management. 2. Use the official practice materials The Scheme provides practice assessments, hints and tips videos and technical checks. These resources can help applicants understand what to expect. 3. Prepare examples from your experience Think about situations where you have demonstrated qualities such as: Leadership Teamwork Communication Problem-solving Adaptability Initiative Resilience Working with others Responding to change These examples do not necessarily have to come from formal employment. 4. Prepare for video responses Because Stage 2 includes video questions, applicants should become comfortable explaining their experiences and motivations clearly on camera. 5. Check your technology Make sure your: Camera works Microphone works Internet connection is reliable Computer is suitable for the assessment platform Assessment environment is appropriate The NHS provides technical checks as part of its preparation process. 6. Apply early Although the final deadline is 28 October at 11:30am , applicants are encouraged to apply early because there are multiple assessment stages after the initial application. Learn more HERE Frequently Asked Questions Can final-year students apply? Yes. Final-year students can apply if they meet the Scheme s requirements and have their final confirmed degree classification of at least 2:2 by mid-August 2027. Is a specific degree subject required? For General Management, Human Resources, Finance and Digital – Health Informatics, the minimum requirement is a 2:2 degree in any subject. Engineering and Estates Management has specific engineering-degree requirements. Do I need previous work experience? No specific work experience is required. However, paid or unpaid experience can provide useful examples during the recruitment process. Can current NHS employees apply? Yes. Current NHS employees can apply as in-service trainees, but they must meet the same academic and right-to-work requirements. Is there an age limit? No. The NHS states that there is no age limit for applicants. Do I need the right to work in the UK? Yes. Applicants must have the right to work in the UK for the entire duration of the Scheme. When does the 2027 Scheme begin? Successful candidates are expected to join on the first Monday of September 2027. Does completing the Scheme guarantee a permanent NHS job? No. Trainees are employed during the Scheme, and the NHS provides support with finding a first substantive NHS role afterwards, but a particular job is not guaranteed. When is the application deadline? Applications for 2027 entry close on 28 October 2026 at 11:30am . Conclusion The NHS Graduate Management Training Scheme 2027 provides an opportunity for eligible graduates, final-year students and current NHS employees to develop their leadership and management careers while gaining practical experience within the NHS. The recruitment process places considerable emphasis on potential, strengths, motivation and individual capability , rather than requiring applicants to come from one particular academic discipline or have a specific professional background. For most pathways, a 2:2 degree in any subject is sufficient academically, while Engineering and Estates Management has separate engineering requirements. Applicants must also have the right to work in the UK for the entire duration of the Scheme. The selection process progresses from the application and Future Potential Assessment through the NHS GMTS Alignment Assessment and finally to the Virtual Assessment Centre. Successful candidates then go through placement allocation, pre-employment checks and onboarding before beginning the Scheme in September 2027. With applications currently open, prospective applicants should review the requirements for their preferred pathway, make use of the available preparation resources and submit their application before the 28 October 2026 at 11:30am deadline . title: Royal Society Career Development Fellowship 2027: Up to £703,800 for Early-Career Black Researchers in STEM
summary: The Royal Society Career Development Fellowship 2027 is a four-year postdoctoral research fellowship designed to support talented early-career scientists from underrepresented backgrounds as they establish and develop independent research careers in the United Kingdom. The fellowship provides substantial research funding, alongside structured mentoring, training, networking and career-development opportunities. The scheme is particularly intended to support researchers from Black heritage backgrounds, including mixed Black backgrounds , during the transition from postgraduate study into the early stages of a postdoctoral research career. The current fellowship round is open , with applications closing on 18 November 2026 . The scheme is intended for researchers whose work falls within the Royal Society s natural sciences remit, including areas such as biological research and biomedical sciences, chemistry, engineering, mathematics and physics. About the Royal Society Career Development Fellowship The Career Development Fellowship (CDF) is a four-year postdoctoral research fellowship created to support the retention and progression of researchers from underrepresented backgrounds within STEM. The fellowship combines financial support for research with a comprehensive programme of mentoring, training and networking . Its broader purpose is to help award holders establish a successful research career within a UK institution and strengthen their long-term participation in science, technology, engineering and mathematics. According to the Royal Society, the scheme was developed following cross-sector discussions and research examining trends in the representation of ethnic minority researchers across higher education. This work identified a particular need for support for researchers from Black, Mixed Black African, Black Caribbean and other Black heritage backgrounds , especially those making the transition from postgraduate education into the early postdoctoral stage. The current programme is being offered as a pilot focused on researchers from Black heritage backgrounds . The Royal Society states that, if the pilot is successful, the programme may subsequently be broadened to other underrepresented groups. What the Career Development Fellowship Aims to Achieve The Royal Society Career Development Fellowship is structured around several objectives: Supporting talented early-career researchers from underrepresented backgrounds as they take the first steps toward establishing their research in a UK institution. Giving researchers the opportunity to undertake high-quality, curiosity-led research . Providing promising researchers with mentoring, networking, training and other forms of professional support. Helping researchers from underrepresented groups pursue long-term careers in STEM. Contributing to the development and strengthening of the UK scientific workforce. The Royal Society also highlights the importance of diversity in achieving excellence in STEM. The organisation states that bringing together researchers with different backgrounds, perspectives and experiences can contribute to innovation and creativity in science. What the Fellowship Offers Successful applicants can apply for up to £703,800 over four years . The funding can support several components of the fellowship and research programme, including: Research Fellow salary: A contribution toward the Research Fellow s salary and associated on-costs at 80%. Directly allocated costs: Funding for eligible directly allocated costs at 80%. Research expenses: Research expenses can be covered at 100%. Relocation and visa costs: Eligible applicants can request relocation and visa costs for themselves and their dependants, including a partner and children, in addition to the £703,800 grant cap over four years. Beyond the financial award, the fellowship includes a tailored programme of training, mentoring and engagement designed to help researchers strengthen their professional and research careers. Royal Society Research Fellows can also access additional career-development and engagement opportunities, including training related to leadership, science communication and public engagement , as well as activities coordinated by the Society s science policy and schools engagement teams. Flexible Support for Researchers The fellowship also recognises that researchers may have different personal and professional circumstances. The Royal Society provides flexibility that can accommodate arrangements such as: Part-time working Sabbaticals Secondments Maternity leave Paternity leave Shared parental leave Adoptive leave Extended sick leave There is also provision for financial support for childcare costs arising from activities such as attending conferences, collaborative research visits and invited talks. This means the fellowship is not solely focused on providing research funding; it also incorporates measures intended to support researchers in managing different circumstances while developing their careers. Who Can Apply? The Royal Society Career Development Fellowship has specific eligibility requirements. Prospective applicants should carefully review these requirements before beginning an application. 1. Black heritage background Applicants must self-identify as being from a Black heritage background , including a mixed Black background. The current pilot specifically focuses on researchers from Black heritage backgrounds. 2. UK connection Applicants must satisfy at least one of the specified UK-connection requirements. You can be eligible if you are: A UK national ; or Someone who has completed part of their education in the UK through an undergraduate, Master s or PhD degree ; or Someone who holds or has previously held a postdoctoral researcher position in the UK . Importantly, applicants do not necessarily have to be UK-domiciled. The Royal Society states that both UK- and non-UK-domiciled researchers who intend to conduct their research in the UK can apply. Applicants can be of any nationality , provided they satisfy the scheme s other eligibility requirements. Researchers who require a visa are also eligible to apply for a Global Talent Visa through the fast-track endorsement process described by the Royal Society. 3. Academic and career stage Applicants must have a PhD , or be expected to have obtained one by the time the fellowship funding begins. They must also have less than 24 months of postdoctoral experience . This makes the programme particularly relevant to researchers who are at the early stage of their postdoctoral careers and are seeking to establish themselves as independent researchers. 4. Research discipline The applicant s research must fall within the Royal Society s natural sciences remit . The eligible areas include, but are not limited to: Biological research Biomedical sciences Chemistry Engineering Mathematics Physics Applicants should consult the Royal Society s detailed subject-group information to determine whether their specific research area falls within the fellowship s supported disciplines. Nationality and Geographic Eligibility The fellowship is open to researchers from any nationality , provided they meet the scheme s eligibility conditions. Therefore, the opportunity is not restricted exclusively to UK citizens. International researchers can also apply if they have the required UK connection through their education or postdoctoral research experience and intend to carry out their research in the UK. For example, a researcher from an African country could potentially qualify if they meet the fellowship s Black heritage requirement, academic and postdoctoral experience requirements, natural sciences research requirements, and one of the specified UK-connection requirements. Research Focus and Academic Areas One of the important features of the Career Development Fellowship is its emphasis on high-quality, curiosity-led research . The fellowship is intended for researchers whose work falls within the Royal Society s natural sciences remit rather than being restricted to one specific scientific discipline. This broad remit means that eligible researchers working in fields such as mathematics, physics, engineering, chemistry, biological sciences and biomedical sciences may potentially find the fellowship relevant to their research careers. Royal Society and Alzheimer s Society Career Development Fellowship The scheme also includes a partnership between the Royal Society and Alzheimer s Society . Under this partnership, funding is available for an applicant undertaking research that is directly relevant to dementia , excluding clinical and interventional studies on humans. This provides an additional route within the fellowship for eligible researchers whose research directly addresses dementia-related questions within the stated research restrictions. Application Timeline for the 2027 Fellowship Applicants should take note of the key dates for the current round: Application milestone Date Applications open 22 September 2026 Application deadline 18 November 2026 Decision by 30 June 2027 The application deadline is therefore 18 November 2026 . Applications should be submitted before the closing date through the Royal Society s grant management system. How to Apply Applications are submitted through Flexi-Grant , the Royal Society s application and grant-management system. Applicants should ensure that they carefully review the fellowship s scheme notes and eligibility requirements before submitting an application. The assessment process is overseen by the Career Development Fellowship panel . Applicants who are shortlisted will be invited to an in-person interview at the Royal Society . During the interview, shortlisted applicants are expected to demonstrate the importance and scientific validity of their proposed research. The Royal Society also provides application tips to help prospective applicants understand the expectations of the fellowship application. APPLY HERE Important Things Applicants Should Prepare Because this is a competitive postdoctoral research fellowship, prospective applicants should pay close attention to the relationship between their academic background, research proposal and career-development objectives. Before applying, applicants should ensure that they can clearly demonstrate: Eligibility for the Black heritage requirement under the current pilot. A PhD or expected PhD completion by the time funding begins. Less than 24 months of postdoctoral experience . A qualifying UK connection through nationality, education or postdoctoral research experience. Research within the Royal Society s natural sciences remit. A clear research direction suitable for the fellowship s focus on high-quality, curiosity-led research. A credible pathway toward establishing a successful research career in the UK. Applicants should also review the official scheme notes because the detailed eligibility, funding and assessment requirements should be treated as the authoritative basis for preparing an application. Training, Mentoring and Networking Opportunities An important part of the Career Development Fellowship is that it goes beyond conventional research funding. Successful fellows receive access to a programme designed to support their wider professional development. This includes mentoring, training and networking opportunities , all intended to help researchers build the skills, professional connections and experience required for a sustainable scientific career. Additional Royal Society opportunities can include professional development in areas such as: Leadership Science communication Public engagement Research networking Engagement with science policy Engagement with schools and wider audiences These opportunities are intended to complement the research component of the fellowship and help researchers develop beyond their immediate scientific projects. Click HERE to sign up to the Information Session. Funding for Relocation and Visas International researchers should pay particular attention to the fellowship s provisions for relocation and immigration-related costs. The Royal Society states that relocation and visa costs for fellows and their dependants can be requested in addition to the £703,800 four-year grant cap. This can be particularly relevant to researchers who are currently based outside the United Kingdom and intend to relocate for the fellowship. The Royal Society also states that applicants who require a visa may be eligible for a Global Talent Visa through the fast-track endorsement process. Fellowship Duration The Career Development Fellowship lasts for four years . This provides successful researchers with a substantial period in which to conduct their research, develop their academic profile, establish professional networks and participate in structured career-development activities. The four-year structure is particularly relevant to the fellowship s broader objective of helping early-career researchers move toward establishing a sustainable research career within a UK institution. Why Early-Career Researchers Should Review This Opportunity The fellowship brings together several components that are relevant to researchers at the early postdoctoral stage. Rather than providing research funding alone, it combines: Up to £703,800 over four years Support toward the fellow s salary Funding for eligible research expenses Directly allocated costs Potential relocation and visa support Mentoring Training Networking Leadership and professional development Science communication and public engagement opportunities Flexible arrangements for certain personal circumstances The programme is specifically designed around the career-development needs of researchers from an underrepresented group in STEM, with the current pilot focused on researchers from Black heritage backgrounds. Key Facts at a Glance Opportunity: Royal Society Career Development Fellowship 2027 Provider: The Royal Society Category: Fellowship Career stage: Early career/postdoctoral Duration: Four years Maximum funding: Up to £703,800 Application opens: 22 September 2026 Deadline: 18 November 2026 Decision by: 30 June 2027 Location: United Kingdom Research areas: Natural sciences, including biological research and biomedical sciences, chemistry, engineering, mathematics and physics Target group: Researchers from Black heritage backgrounds, including mixed Black backgrounds Nationality: Applicants can be of any nationality, subject to the scheme s UK-connection and other eligibility requirements Domicile: Both UK- and non-UK-domiciled researchers may be eligible Application platform: Royal Society Flexi-Grant Interview: Shortlisted applicants will be invited to an in-person interview at the Royal Society. Application Deadline The deadline to apply for the Royal Society Career Development Fellowship 2027 is 18 November 2026 . Applicants should not wait until the final day to begin preparing their applications. Prospective candidates should first confirm that they meet every eligibility requirement, review the official scheme notes, develop their research proposal and prepare the supporting information required through the Royal Society s Flexi-Grant system. Visit HERE for more information about the Royal Society Career Development Fellowship 2027. Conclusion The Royal Society Career Development Fellowship 2027 provides a four-year funding and professional-development opportunity for eligible early-career researchers from Black heritage backgrounds who are seeking to establish research careers in the United Kingdom. With funding of up to £703,800 , support for research expenses and salary-related costs, potential relocation and visa funding, and access to structured mentoring, training and networking, the fellowship is designed to provide both financial and professional support during an important stage of an academic researcher s career. The opportunity is open to applicants of any nationality who satisfy the relevant eligibility conditions, including the required UK connection, PhD and postdoctoral-experience requirements, Black heritage criterion and natural sciences research requirement. Both UK- and non-UK-domiciled researchers intending to conduct their research in the UK can be eligible. Researchers interested in applying should carefully examine the official scheme requirements and prepare their applications well ahead of the 18 November 2026 deadline . Official Application and Further Information Applicants can access the Royal Society s fellowship information, scheme notes and application system through the official Royal Society resources provided in the source material. Pro tip: Before submitting your application, carefully check the detailed scheme notes against your nationality or UK connection, PhD completion status, postdoctoral experience, research discipline and Black heritage eligibility. This can help you confirm your eligibility before investing substantial time in the full application. Discover more global Fellowship opportunities on Opportunities for Youth HERE . title: Halcyon Open Application 2026: Apply Year-Round to Join a Global Community of Impact-Driven Founders
summary: Entrepreneurs building businesses designed to create meaningful social, environmental or economic impact can now apply to Halcyon’s founder community through its new year-round open application process . Instead of waiting for a single annual application deadline, eligible ventures can submit an Eligibility Application at any time of the year and have their applications reviewed on a rolling basis. The new application model is designed to make Halcyon’s founder selection process more accessible, flexible and open throughout the year. Rather than requiring every venture to apply directly to a specific fellowship at a fixed time, Halcyon has introduced a two-step application process that begins with a short eligibility application. If a venture meets Halcyon’s criteria and a future fellowship is considered a suitable match, the venture may be invited to complete a more detailed Invitational Application . For entrepreneurs developing solutions with the potential to generate positive impact at scale, this creates a pathway to be considered for future Halcyon fellowship opportunities without having to wait for a particular fellowship application window to open. What Is the Halcyon Open Application? The Halcyon Open Application is a year-round entry point for impact-driven ventures interested in becoming part of Halcyon’s founder community. Under the updated process, entrepreneurs begin by completing a relatively short Eligibility Application . This first stage allows Halcyon to determine whether a venture is potentially suitable for its programmes. The application asks applicants to provide information about areas such as The venture s mission The stage of the venture Its impact focus The nature of the solution being developed The venture s potential fit with Halcyon s programmes Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis , meaning entrepreneurs do not have to wait for one specific annual deadline to submit the first-stage application. If the venture meets Halcyon s eligibility criteria, its application can remain relevant for consideration when a fellowship opens that aligns with the venture. How the New Halcyon Application Process Works The application process consists of two main stages. Step 1: Submit the Eligibility Application The first step is an Eligibility Application , which is open throughout the year. This initial application is designed to help Halcyon quickly assess whether a venture may be a suitable fit for its programmes. Applicants will be asked basic questions about their venture, including its: Mission Development stage Impact focus General approach and solution Potential fit with Halcyon s programmes The first stage is intentionally more accessible than a full fellowship application. Once submitted, applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. Important requirement: Apply only once. Applicants should pay close attention to one important rule. The Eligibility Application can only be submitted once . Halcyon states that duplicate applications will be automatically rejected . Entrepreneurs should therefore make sure their first submission is accurate, complete and carefully prepared before submitting it. This is particularly important because applicants should not treat the eligibility form as a preliminary form that can simply be resubmitted repeatedly with different information. Step 2: The Invitational Application The second stage is significantly more detailed and is available by invitation only . If Halcyon determines that a venture meets its eligibility criteria and a relevant fellowship programme becomes available, the venture may receive an invitation to complete the second-stage application. The Invitational Application gives Halcyon an opportunity to understand the venture in much greater depth. Applicants can expect this stage to examine areas such as The founding team The innovation behind the venture The problem being addressed The venture s impact Scalability Growth potential The founder s vision The venture s broader ambitions Unlike the first-stage application, entrepreneurs cannot simply access the Invitational Application independently. It is reserved for ventures that have first been identified through the Eligibility Application process. What Does Halcyon Look for in Applicants? Halcyon states that its selection committee evaluates applications using four key criteria : 1. Impact The first criterion is the potential of the venture to create meaningful positive impact. Applicants should be able to clearly explain the problem they are addressing and why solving that problem matters. A strong application should make it possible to understand: What challenge the venture is addressing Who is affected by the challenge How the venture s solution responds to the problem What kind of positive change the venture seeks to create How the impact can potentially be demonstrated or measured The impact component is particularly important because Halcyon s founder community is centred on businesses seeking to generate positive influence. 2. Scalability Halcyon also considers the potential for a venture to grow. Scalability involves demonstrating that the solution has the potential to expand beyond its current size, market or initial group of beneficiaries. Applicants should therefore think carefully about questions such as: Can the solution reach more people? Can the business expand into additional markets? What is the potential size of the problem being addressed? What barriers could limit expansion? What would growth look like over the next several years? Entrepreneurs should present a realistic growth vision rather than simply stating that they intend to scale. 3. Innovation Innovation is another central selection criterion. Applicants should communicate what makes their approach different and why their solution offers a meaningful response to an existing challenge. Innovation could relate to: The technology being developed The business model The delivery model The product or service The way an existing problem is being approached A new method of reaching underserved communities A new way of generating measurable impact The key is to demonstrate what is distinctive about the venture and how that distinction contributes to solving the identified problem. 4. Talent The fourth criterion is talent . This allows the selection committee to assess the people behind the venture, including their ability, experience, ambition and potential to execute the proposed vision. Entrepreneurs should therefore make their application about more than just the product. The application should also demonstrate: Why the founders are equipped to address the problem What relevant experience the team possesses What the founders have already accomplished How the team complements one another Why the founders are committed to the venture Why they have the ambition to grow the solution Pitch Deck Is Now Required One of the most important changes highlighted in the application information is that applicants are now required to upload a pitch deck of up to 15 slides . This means entrepreneurs should prepare a clear and professionally structured pitch deck before submitting their application. A strong pitch deck can help communicate the venture s story in a way that is easy for the selection committee to understand. While the specific content can vary depending on the venture, entrepreneurs may consider using their pitch deck to clearly present: The problem The target population or market The proposed solution How the solution works The innovation behind the approach The business or operating model Evidence of traction Impact achieved so far Growth and scalability potential Market opportunity Competitive landscape Team and relevant expertise Future growth strategy Financial or business milestones The long-term vision Applicants should ensure that every slide adds useful information and supports the overall story of the venture. Because the limit is 15 slides , entrepreneurs should avoid filling the presentation with excessive text. The strongest deck structure is generally one in which the problem, solution, impact, traction, team and future opportunity can be understood quickly. Optional One-Minute Video In addition to the required pitch deck, applicants may also upload a one-minute video describing their venture . Although the video is optional, it can provide an opportunity to communicate elements that may be difficult to convey through written answers alone. The video can help founders demonstrate: Their passion for the problem they are solving Their vision for the venture Their ability to communicate clearly The human story behind the business Why the problem matters Why they are committed to creating positive impact A one-minute video should remain focused. Rather than attempting to explain every detail of the business, founders can use the limited time to communicate the core problem, the solution, the impact and their vision. Why the Year-Round Application Matters One of the biggest changes in Halcyon s process is the move away from a traditional fixed application cycle for the initial eligibility stage. Previously, entrepreneurs might have had to wait for a particular fellowship application to open before submitting their venture for consideration. The new model allows founders to submit the Eligibility Application at any time during the year . This means entrepreneurs can begin the process when they are ready rather than waiting for a specific fellowship deadline. It also allows Halcyon to connect eligible ventures with future fellowships that are relevant to their areas of work. For founders developing impact-driven businesses, this can make the application process more flexible. There Is No Fixed Annual Deadline for Step 1 Unlike many fellowship and accelerator opportunities, the Halcyon Eligibility Application does not have a single annual deadline . The application is described as being open year-round , with submissions reviewed on a rolling basis. Therefore, the opportunity is particularly useful for founders who may not currently be ready for a particular fellowship but want their venture to be considered for future programmes. However, applicants should understand the distinction between the two stages: Step 1: Open year-round Step 2: Opens only by invitation when an aligned fellowship becomes available The absence of a fixed deadline for Step 1 does not mean that every venture will automatically progress to Step 2. What Happens If Your Venture Is Not Selected? Halcyon s process also provides an important clarification for applicants. If a venture is not selected during the Eligibility Application stage, Halcyon indicates that the venture is not considered a fit for any of its fellowships based on the eligibility assessment. This makes the first-stage application an important screening process rather than simply a registration form. Entrepreneurs should therefore take time to understand Halcyon s eligibility requirements before submitting their application. Who Should Consider Applying? The Halcyon Open Application is designed for founders and ventures , rather than individual applicants seeking traditional educational scholarships or employment opportunities. It is particularly relevant to entrepreneurs who are developing businesses or solutions with a clear impact mission. Potential applicants may include founders working on solutions related to areas such as Climate Health Equity Social innovation Environmental sustainability Technology for positive impact Economic inclusion Community development Other significant social or environmental challenges The exact areas of focus can depend on the fellowship programme that becomes available. Halcyon s past programming has included ventures from multiple countries and regions. For example, its 2024 Climate Fellowship received applications from 69 countries across all continents except Antarctica, demonstrating the international reach of its fellowship programming. However, applicants should distinguish this historical cohort information from the eligibility requirements of a specific future fellowship. How to Prepare a Strong Halcyon Application Entrepreneurs interested in applying should begin preparing well before submitting their Eligibility Application. 1. Clearly define the problem. Start by identifying the specific problem the venture is addressing. Avoid using broad statements that do not demonstrate the scale or nature of the problem. Instead, explain: What the problem is Who experiences it Why existing approaches are insufficient How significant the problem is What evidence demonstrates the need for your solution 2. Explain your solution clearly. The selection committee needs to understand what the venture actually does. Explain the product, service, technology or business model in straightforward language. Avoid unnecessary technical terminology unless it is essential to understanding the innovation. 3. Demonstrate impact Since impact is one of Halcyon s four stated selection criteria, founders should provide evidence where possible. Examples could include: Number of people reached Communities served Revenue generated while delivering impact Environmental outcomes Health outcomes Educational outcomes Jobs created Improvements in access or affordability Partnerships established Other measurable results 4. Demonstrate traction If the venture is already operating, provide evidence showing what has been achieved. This could include: Customers Users Revenue Partnerships Pilot programmes Contracts Product launches Geographic expansion Investment Awards Measurable impact Founders at an earlier stage should explain what has already been validated and what evidence supports the business model. 5. Explain the innovation. Don t simply describe the venture as innovative. Explain why it is innovative. Identify the specific element that distinguishes the venture from existing solutions. 6. Demonstrate scalability Explain what growth could look like. Applicants should show that they have thought about: Market size Customer growth Geographic expansion Operational capacity Partnerships Technology Funding requirements Team growth Potential barriers to expansion 7. Introduce the founding team. Use the application and pitch deck to explain why the team is capable of executing the vision. Highlight relevant: Professional experience Technical skills Entrepreneurial experience Industry knowledge Community experience Previous achievements 8. Prepare the pitch deck carefully. Because the pitch deck is now required and is limited to 15 slides , founders should make every slide purposeful. The deck should tell a coherent story rather than functioning as a collection of unrelated information. 9. Consider adding the one-minute video. The optional video can add personality to the application and allow founders to communicate their motivation directly. Keep it concise, authentic and focused on the venture. 10. Submit only once. Because duplicate Eligibility Applications are automatically rejected, founders should carefully review their information before pressing submit. Step 2: Prepare your venture information Gather information about: Your mission Venture stage Impact Innovation Scalability Founding team Vision Step 3: Prepare your pitch deck. Create a pitch deck of no more than 15 slides , as required by the current application process. Step 4: Consider recording the optional video Prepare a one-minute video that introduces the venture and communicates the founders passion and vision. Step 5: Submit the Eligibility Application Submit the first-stage application through Halcyon s application platform. Remember that the Eligibility Application can only be submitted once. Step 6: Wait for the rolling review Halcyon reviews Eligibility Applications on a rolling basis. Step 7: Await a potential invitation If the venture meets the criteria and a suitable fellowship opens, Halcyon may invite the founder to complete the more detailed Invitational Application. Step 8: Complete the Invitational Application If invited, provide more detailed information about the venture, team, innovation, scalability, impact and vision. Frequently Asked Questions Does the Halcyon Open Application have a deadline? There is no fixed deadline stated for the Eligibility Application . The application is open year-round and reviewed on a rolling basis. However, individual fellowship programmes may have their own application windows and requirements. Can I apply more than once? No. Halcyon states that the Eligibility Application can only be submitted once. Duplicate applications are automatically rejected. Is the second application open to everyone? No. The second-stage Invitational Application is by invitation only . Is a pitch deck required? Yes. The current application information states that applicants are required to upload a pitch deck of up to 15 slides . Is the one-minute video mandatory? No. The one-minute video is optional. What does Halcyon look for? The selection committee evaluates applications using four criteria: Impact, Scalability, Innovation and Talent . Is this an individual scholarship? No. This opportunity is designed for entrepreneurs and impact-driven ventures seeking consideration for Halcyon s fellowship programmes. Can international founders apply? Halcyon s fellowship programming has demonstrated an international reach, including applicants and fellows from numerous countries. However, eligibility can vary by specific fellowship, so founders should check the requirements for the fellowship to which they are ultimately invited. The first stage focuses on determining whether a venture is a potential fit based on its mission, stage and impact focus. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, while ventures that meet the criteria may later be invited to complete a more comprehensive application when an appropriate fellowship becomes available. Applicants should pay particular attention to Halcyon s four selection criteria: Impact, Scalability, Innovation and Talent . The current process also requires applicants to submit a pitch deck of up to 15 slides, while a one-minute video may be included as an optional way to communicate the venture s story and the founders vision. title: Star Catcher Summer 2027 Paid Internships: Apply for Engineering, Marketing and Communications Roles in the Space Industry
summary: Star Catcher is offering paid, full-time Summer 2027 internships for undergraduate students, graduate students, and recent graduates interested in contributing to the development of next-generation space energy infrastructure. The internship program provides participants with an opportunity to gain practical experience at a high-growth space technology company working toward building what it describes as the first power grid in space . Applications are currently open for available Summer 2027 internship positions, with opportunities spanning engineering, science, business, marketing, communications, and related disciplines. Successful interns will work on real-world challenges, collaborate with experienced professionals, and contribute to projects involving the systems and infrastructure needed to support an emerging orbital economy. Deadline: November 15, 2026. About the Star Catcher Summer 2027 Internship Program The Star Catcher internship program is designed for students and recent graduates who want to move beyond classroom learning and gain hands-on experience in the rapidly developing space technology sector. As an intern, you will have the opportunity to participate in work that directly contributes to Star Catcher s efforts to develop space-based power infrastructure. Rather than being limited to observational or administrative responsibilities, the program emphasizes practical work, rapid learning, ownership, and exposure to real engineering and operational challenges. The company is seeking students from a broad range of academic and professional backgrounds. This makes the program relevant not only to traditional aerospace and engineering students, but also to candidates studying computer science, physics, business, marketing, communications, and related fields. The internships are paid and full-time , giving selected candidates the opportunity to gain professional experience while working alongside teams involved in building emerging space technology. What Will Interns Work On? Star Catcher describes its mission as building the systems needed to establish a power grid in space. Interns will therefore have the opportunity to contribute to work connected to space technology, engineering, business operations, communications, and the development of the company s broader commercial direction. Depending on the position, interns may become involved in: Engineering systems and technologies designed for space-based power infrastructure. Research and technical problem-solving. Development and analysis of spacecraft-related systems. Software and computational projects. Optical and electrical engineering applications. Business development activities. Market research and analysis. Proposal development. Marketing initiatives. Corporate and external communications. Content creation and storytelling. Event organization. Graphic design and visual communications. Photography and videography. Motion graphics and other creative projects. Cross-functional projects involving multiple teams. The specific responsibilities will depend on the internship position and the applicant s academic background, skills, and experience. Available Internship Areas Star Catcher is looking for qualified undergraduate and graduate students to work across several disciplines. The available areas include: 1. Aerospace Engineering Aerospace Engineering interns can gain experience working in an industry focused on spacecraft and space-based infrastructure. Candidates with an interest in spacecraft systems, aerospace technologies, and related engineering challenges may find this area particularly relevant. 2. Mechanical Engineering Mechanical Engineering students can contribute their technical knowledge to projects involving mechanical systems and components. The role may provide exposure to the practical application of mechanical engineering principles in the space industry. 3. Electrical Engineering Electrical Engineering opportunities are aimed at students interested in electrical systems and technologies supporting space-based infrastructure. This area can provide practical experience applying electrical engineering knowledge to real-world space technology challenges. 4. Optical Engineering Optical Engineering interns can contribute to work involving optical systems and technologies relevant to space applications. This opportunity is particularly suited to students with an academic or project background in optical engineering or closely related disciplines. 5. Computer Science Computer Science students can explore opportunities involving software, programming, computational problem-solving, and technology development. Candidates with experience in programming languages and technical tools may be able to apply their skills to practical space technology projects. 6. Physics Physics students can apply analytical and scientific knowledge to real-world problems within the space technology environment. The discipline provides a foundation for understanding and addressing technical challenges associated with advanced space systems. 7. Marketing and Communications The program also includes opportunities for students studying or experienced in Marketing and Communications. Candidates in this area may work on activities such as: Market research. Writing and content development. Communications. Marketing campaigns. Event organization. Graphic design. Photography and videography. Motion graphics. Other communication and creative projects. This makes the program relevant to students who want to combine communication, creativity, technology, and the rapidly developing space industry. 8. Business Development Business Development interns can gain exposure to commercial and strategic activities within a high-growth technology company. Candidates interested in identifying opportunities, researching markets, developing proposals, and supporting business growth may be considered for relevant positions. Who Can Apply? Star Catcher is seeking qualified undergraduate and graduate students of all backgrounds , as well as recent graduates. Applicants should currently be pursuing a Bachelor s or Master s degree in one of the relevant disciplines or have recently graduated from a related program. Relevant fields include: Aerospace Engineering Mechanical Engineering Electrical Engineering Optical Engineering Computer Science Physics Marketing Communications Business Administration Related academic fields Recent graduates may also qualify, depending on the requirements of the particular internship position. Applicants should carefully review the individual position description before applying because specific requirements may vary between engineering, business development, marketing, and communications opportunities. U.S. Citizenship and Space Technology Export Requirements An important eligibility consideration applies to these internships because of the nature of the company s space technology work. Applicants must meet the applicable U.S. government authorization requirements for access to regulated space technology. According to the provided internship information, candidates must be one of the following: A U.S. citizen; A lawful permanent resident of the United States; A protected individual as defined under 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3) ; or An individual eligible to obtain the necessary authorizations from the U.S. Department of State to comply with U.S. government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) . Therefore, international applicants should not assume that being enrolled in a relevant degree program automatically makes them eligible. Applicants should carefully assess their ability to satisfy the applicable export-control and authorization requirements before submitting an application. What Experience Does Star Catcher Look For? Academic qualifications are important, but Star Catcher is also looking for candidates who can demonstrate practical experience, technical ability, communication skills, and an interest in space, technology, and innovation. Ideal candidates may have some combination of the following: Previous Internship or Project Experience Previous internship experience can demonstrate that an applicant has already had exposure to professional environments. Hands-on academic, personal, technical, or extracurricular projects may also help demonstrate the ability to turn theoretical knowledge into practical results. Strong Communication Skills Interns will work with other people and may need to communicate technical or business information clearly. Strong written and verbal communication skills can therefore be valuable across both technical and non-technical positions. Organizational Skills Because interns may work on projects with deadlines and multiple responsibilities, strong organizational and time-management skills can help candidates perform effectively. Independent and Collaborative Working Skills Star Catcher is seeking people who can work independently while also contributing effectively within team-oriented environments. Applicants should be prepared to demonstrate that they can take ownership of assigned responsibilities while collaborating with colleagues. Analytical and Problem-Solving Skills The ability to analyze problems, identify potential solutions, and approach unfamiliar challenges systematically is important for an internship focused on developing new technologies and business opportunities. Engineering Skills and Technical Experience Candidates applying for engineering positions are expected to have relevant technical knowledge and experience. Marketing, Communications and Business Development Skills Candidates interested in non-engineering roles can also demonstrate their suitability through academic coursework and practical experience. Videography. Motion graphics. Business development. Communication strategy. Digital content production. Candidates should demonstrate how their previous experiences have helped them develop practical skills that can be applied in a professional environment. Why Consider an Internship at Star Catcher? The program provides an opportunity to gain professional experience in an emerging area of the space industry while contributing to projects at a high-growth startup. According to Star Catcher, interns can benefit from several aspects of the experience. Direct Exposure to Industry Professionals Interns will have an opportunity to work around experienced professionals and gain exposure to people working on advanced space technology and business challenges. For students interested in aerospace, engineering, computing, physics, communications, business, or technology, this type of experience can provide insight into how emerging technologies move from concepts and research toward practical applications. Gain Space Industry Experience For students hoping to establish careers in the space sector, practical industry experience can provide an opportunity to develop professional skills and gain a better understanding of how the sector operates. Summer 2027: Selected interns are expected to participate in the internship program. How to Apply for Star Catcher Summer 2027 Internships There are separate application routes depending on the type of position you are interested in. Engineering Internships Students interested in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Optical Engineering, Computer Science, Physics, and related technical positions can review the available engineering opportunities and submit their applications through the engineering internship application page. title: Maria Rosario Lazzati Niada Scholarship for Afghan Women 2027–2028: CHF 25,000 Annual Scholarship for Afghan Women to Study a Master’s in Geneva
summary: The Maria Rosario Lazzati Niada Scholarship for Afghan Women is now accepting applications for the 2027–2028 academic year , offering an important postgraduate study opportunity for talented Afghan women who hold a university degree and wish to advance their knowledge in international relations and development . The scholarship is offered in memory of Maria Rosario Lazzati Niada and supports successful candidates to undertake a two-year master’s programme at the Geneva Graduate Institute in Switzerland . The scholarship provides CHF 25,000 per year , making it a substantial source of financial support for an eligible scholar pursuing graduate education abroad. The application deadline for the scholarship is 11:59 PM on October 26, 2026 . Maria Rosario Lazzati Niada Scholarship for Afghan Women The Maria Rosario Lazzati Niada Scholarship was established to support talented Afghan women with university-level education who want to further their academic knowledge and professional opportunities in the fields of international relations and development . Successful scholarship beneficiaries will enrol in a two-year master s programme at the Geneva Graduate Institute , a graduate institution based in Geneva, Switzerland. The scholarship is specifically designed around the educational needs and circumstances of Afghan women and seeks to expand opportunities for them to pursue university education abroad. The Geneva Graduate Institute states that its master s programmes can provide pathways toward careers in areas such as academia, diplomacy, international organisations, non-governmental organisations and international corporate organisations. Scholarship Details at a Glance Detail Information Scholarship Name Maria Rosario Lazzati Niada Scholarship for Afghan Women Academic Year 2027–2028 Study Level Postgraduate / Master s Duration Two years Study Location Geneva, Switzerland Institution Geneva Graduate Institute Annual Scholarship Amount CHF 25,000 Field Focus International Relations and Development Target Group Afghan women with a university degree Scholarship Deadline October 26, 2026, at 11:59 PM Institute Application Deadline for the Selected Candidate January 15 English Proficiency Required at the Geneva Graduate Institute application stage Academic References Two required at the Geneva Graduate Institute application stage The scholarship itself is awarded for two years. However, continuation into the second year is subject to the beneficiary preparing a report at the end of the first year and providing evidence of successful academic progress. The scholarship is then renewed based on this review. What Is the Maria Rosario Lazzati Niada Scholarship? The scholarship was created in memory of Maria Rosario Lazzati Niada (18 March 1954–2 February 2022) . According to the Geneva Graduate Institute, Maria Rosario was a high school teacher of history and literature who graduated Magna Cum Laude from the State University of Milan with a degree in the History of Christianity. Her academic interests included the condition of women. Her university thesis on witchcraft later developed into the book La Stregoneria , written with historians S. Abbiati and A. Agnoletto and published by Mondadori in 1984. The book examined persecution between the 13th and 17th centuries and was based on historical trial documents. Her commitment to women s education also extended beyond academic research. In 2005, Maria Rosario played a major role in establishing the Comitato Arghosha Faraway Schools , a charity focused on women s education in Afghanistan. The organisation subsequently supported the construction of 15 schools serving approximately 8,000 pupils from grades 1 to 12 . According to the Geneva Graduate Institute, approximately 5,500 of these pupils were girls , while 10 of the schools were built specifically for girls who had little or no access to educational facilities. The organisation also supported: Literacy courses for approximately 500 adult women . 28 university scholarships for talented girls at universities in Kabul. The development and implementation of educational initiatives in different parts of Afghanistan. Until 2019, Maria Rosario reportedly travelled to Afghanistan each year to assess the implementation of projects and help plan future initiatives. The scholarship therefore continues a broader legacy centred on education and opportunities for Afghan women. What Does the Scholarship Offer? One of the most significant features of this opportunity is its financial support. CHF 25,000 per year The Maria Rosario Lazzati Niada Scholarship provides an annual scholarship amount of 25,000 Swiss francs . Since the scholarship is structured as a two-year award, it can provide substantial financial assistance throughout the master s programme, subject to renewal for the second year. The scholarship is particularly significant because it is designed to support eligible Afghan women pursuing postgraduate education outside Afghanistan. Two years of master s-level study Successful candidates will undertake a two-year master s programme at the Geneva Graduate Institute . The scholarship is therefore intended for candidates seeking advanced academic training rather than short-term training or undergraduate education. Academic and professional development The opportunity is focused on strengthening knowledge in international relations and development . The Institute notes that master s-level education can create pathways into academic and diplomatic careers as well as employment with international organisations, non-governmental organisations and international companies. Who Can Apply for the Maria Rosario Lazzati Niada Scholarship? The scholarship is specifically intended for Afghan women who already hold a university degree and wish to pursue master s-level studies. The official scholarship description identifies the target applicants as talented Afghan women with a university degree who want to improve their knowledge in international relations and development. Basic eligibility profile Applicants should therefore fall within the following broad category: Women applicants Afghan applicants Applicants who hold a university degree Applicants interested in pursuing master s-level study Applicants seeking further academic development in areas connected to international relations and development Applicants who can prepare the required scholarship application documentation. Applicants who, if selected by the scholarship committee, can subsequently complete the Geneva Graduate Institute admission process. The official scholarship information does not state a particular race requirement . The eligibility criterion is specifically framed around being an Afghan woman , rather than race. In geographic terms, the opportunity is therefore targeted specifically at Afghan women , rather than being a scholarship open to women from all African, Asian, European or other continents. There is also no age limit stated in the scholarship information provided by the Geneva Graduate Institute. What Documents Are Required? Applicants need to prepare several important documents before submitting their scholarship application. According to the official 2027–2028 scholarship flyer, applicants must include: 1. Motivation letter The motivation letter should explain several important aspects of the applicant s plans. It should cover: Why the applicant is applying for the Maria Rosario Lazzati Niada Scholarship. Which Geneva Graduate Institute master s programme the applicant wants to pursue. Why the applicant has selected the Geneva Graduate Institute. The applicant s financial needs. The applicant s plans after graduation. A strong motivation letter should therefore connect the applicant s educational background, proposed master s programme, career objectives and financial circumstances in a coherent way. 2. Curriculum vitae Applicants must submit a CV outlining their academic background, professional experience, relevant skills, achievements and other qualifications. 3. University diplomas and qualifications Applicants must provide copies of their university diplomas and qualifications obtained . This is particularly important because the scholarship is designed for women who already possess university-level education and are seeking postgraduate study. 4. Official academic transcripts Applicants must also submit official academic transcripts showing their coursework, grades and the corresponding credit values.
